proposal.name: Let each issue and project choose its coding agent

plan.name: Let each issue and project choose its coding agent
plan.summary: An issue picks its coding agent with an `Agent: codex` or `Agent: claude-code` line, read as its Project: line is (outside code blocks, the first one counting, trimmed of backticks and lowercased), else through its project's manifest's new `agent` field (project.Manifest.Agent, `json:"agent,omitempty"`), else it gets the watcher's own agent; a new project's proposal carries its issue's line from the draft (formalize.Proposal.Agent, which Proposal.Manifest writes for a new project only), so the project's manifest records it, while an amendment keeps its project's manifest as it is (D-0046), and scope, unchanged, now refuses a pull request that adds, changes or takes out an existing project's agent (D-0086). factory.Factory gains `Agent`, the name of the agent its Formalizer, Builder and Plumbing run and every issue's default (empty is claude-code), and `Agents map[string]Runners`, the other agents the watcher can run, each a `Runners{Formalizer, Builder, Plumbing}` declared in a new internal/factory/agents.go, which also reads the line and picks an issue's agent; every agent run for an issue is its agent's: the draft of its statements, its plan or its plan of issues, and the build of its project or plan, whose second agent's review the builder makes with that same agent (D-0087, D-0108), and a build whose agent the watcher can't run fails before any run is recorded, naming the agent, as a watcher that can't build plumbing fails now, and never builds with another. An issue whose agent the watcher can't run, or doesn't know, is answered before anything is drafted, as a plumbing issue on another repository is (D-0121): one unsupported post, labeled invariant:human-review-needed, that names the agent the issue picked and every agent the watcher can run, and says to name one of those in the issue's Agent: line and comment `/invariant revise`. `invariant watch`, `formalize` and `synthesize` take `-agent`, default `claude-code`, and since Codex comes in #153's later issues, each refuses any other value along with its other flags, before anything else runs, exiting 2 with a message that names the value and claude-code, the only agent Invariant can run yet, and the watcher's Claude Code runners run Claude Code for every role, reviews included. SPEC.md gains a bullet, citing D-0028, D-0046, D-0052, D-0121 and D-0129, that says how an issue picks its agent, what a new project's manifest records, `-agent`, which choice wins, that every agent run for the issue is that agent's, and how an agent the watcher can't run is answered, and its slice 14 line says the choice is built (#173) and Codex comes next; the README adds the Agent: line to its table of what an issue can say, `-agent` to its watch step, and the same to its slice 14 line; this touches the trusted base, so a person merges it, and since no decision records how an issue and a project pick their agent yet, whoever merges it records one that refines D-0129 and cites it in that bullet.

tests.name: TestAnIssuesAgentLinePicksTheAgentThatDraftsAndBuilds
tests.says: With codex runnable beside the watcher's own claude-code, an issue's Agent: line picks which of them drafts its statements and builds its code: codex for `Agent: codex`, and for a first `agent: `Codex`` outside code blocks, claude-code for `Agent: claude-code`, and the new project's manifest records the line's agent; with no line, the watcher's own agent does both, and the manifest names no agent.

tests.name: TestAProjectsManifestPicksTheAgentUnlessItsIssueDoes
tests.says: An amendment of a project whose manifest names codex is drafted and built by codex when its issue picks no agent, and by claude-code when its issue says `Agent: claude-code`, and either way the amendment's branch keeps the manifest naming codex.

tests.name: TestAnAgentTheWatcherCantRunGetsOneAnswer
tests.says: An issue that picks codex on a watcher that can't run it, picks an agent no one knows, or amends a project whose manifest names codex, gets one unsupported answer labeled for a person, naming the agent it picked and every agent the watcher can run, and nothing is drafted, recorded, pushed or built, then or on later polls.

tests.name: TestARevisedIssueIsDraftedOnceItPicksAnAgentTheWatcherCanRun
tests.says: A writer's revise on an issue whose agent the watcher can't run gets the same answer and no draft, and once the issue's line names claude-code, a revise drafts it.

tests.name: TestAPlanAndAPlanOfIssuesAreTheIssuesAgents
tests.says: A plumbing issue that says `Agent: codex` is planned by codex's formalizer and built by codex's plan builder, and a PRD that says it has its plan of issues drafted by codex, with the watcher's own agent doing none of it.

tests.name: TestTheWatchersOwnAgentIsTheDefault
tests.says: With codex as the watcher's own agent and claude-code runnable beside it, an issue that picks none is drafted and built by codex and its project's manifest names no agent, while one that picks claude-code is drafted and built by claude-code and its manifest names it; a watcher that runs codex alone answers an issue that picks claude-code, naming both.

tests.name: TestABuildRunsOnlyItsIssuesAgent
tests.says: When the agent of a ratified project or plan is one the watcher can no longer run, its build fails naming that agent, no agent builds, and no build run is recorded; once the watcher can run it again, a writer's retry builds the project with it.

tests.name: TestAPullRequestCantChangeAProjectsAgent
tests.says: Scope refuses a pull request that adds, changes or takes out an existing project's agent in its manifest, alone or with a change to its parameters, and takes a new project whose manifest names its agent.

tests.name: TestTheCommandsTakeTheAgentTheyRun
tests.says: `invariant watch`, `formalize` and `synthesize` each show `-agent`, defaulting to claude-code, and refuse codex and an agent no one knows before anything else runs, exiting 2 with a message that names the agent and claude-code, while `formalize -agent claude-code` goes on past its flags to read its request.

usage.summary: The plan for #173 passed the check on its first run: all 9 acceptance tests fail on the code as it is. An issue picks its agent with an `Agent:` line, else its project's manifest (which a new project's manifest now records), else the watcher's `-agent`; every draft, plan, build and review for the issue uses that agent, and an agent the watcher can't run gets one answer and nothing is drafted or built. It touches the trusted base, so a person merges it, and whoever merges it needs to record a decision refining D-0129 and cite it in the new SPEC bullet.
